body.zh: 回答「哪些物体在哪里」：给每个物体一个类别和一个边界框。分类只给整张图一个或几个类别标签，不说位置；不带类别的框只说了在哪里，没说是什么；分割再把答案细化到每个像素。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲，视觉任务（幻灯片 7）。
body.en: Answers which objects are where: a class and a bounding box for each object. Classification gives the whole image one or a few class labels and says nothing about position; a box without a class says where but not what; segmentation refines the answer down to each pixel. Source: COMP90086 lecture 1, vision tasks (slide 7).

body.zh: 给每个像素标出它属于哪一个具体物体（人-1、人-2）。语义分割只标出每个像素属于哪一类：同一类的几个物体挨在一起时连成一片，数不出个数；一个物体被挡成两块时，实例分割仍把两块标成同一个物体。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲（幻灯片 7、30）。
body.en: Labels each pixel with the particular object it belongs to (person-1, person-2). Semantic segmentation labels only each pixel's class: touching objects of one class merge into one region and cannot be counted; when an occluder cuts one object in two, instance segmentation still gives both pieces one id. Source: COMP90086 lecture 1 (slides 7, 30).

body.zh: 同一类、甚至同一个物体的照片，会因大小和距离、视角和姿态、光照、背景、遮挡而大不相同：几乎每个像素都变了，物体却没有变。所以识别不能靠记住像素，要找对这些无关变化有容忍度的表示。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲，识别为什么难（幻灯片 28）。
body.en: Photos of one class, even of one object, differ greatly with size and distance, viewpoint and pose, lighting, background and occlusion: nearly every pixel changes while the object does not. Recognition therefore cannot memorise pixels; it needs a representation tolerant of these irrelevant changes. Source: COMP90086 lecture 1, why recognition is hard (slide 28).

body.zh: 输入有无关的变化（视角、光照、背景，甚至只改了几个像素的对抗样本）时，输出仍然可靠。一次答对、哪怕置信度很高，也证明不了它；一个反例就能推翻「总能认出」，所以测试集要把每一种变化都覆盖到。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，对抗样本（幻灯片 2–3）。
body.en: A system's output stays reliable when irrelevant things about its input change (viewpoint, lighting, background, even the few altered pixels of an adversarial example). One correct answer, however confident, does not show it; one counterexample refutes 'it always recognises', so a test set must cover each kind of change. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, adversarial examples (slides 2–3).

body.zh: 图形学由物体、材质、光照和相机正向生成图像，是正问题；视觉反过来从图像推回这些东西，是反问题。三维场景投成二维图像丢了一维信息，不同的场景能生成同一张图，所以单凭一张图，有些问题（物体多远、多大，挡住的是什么）没有唯一的答案。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲，视觉与图形学（幻灯片 8）。
body.en: Graphics generates an image forwards from objects, materials, lighting and camera: a forward problem. Vision infers them backwards from the image: an inverse problem. Projecting a 3D scene to a 2D image loses a dimension and different scenes can produce the same image, so from one image alone some questions (how far, how big, what is hidden) have no unique answer. Source: COMP90086 lecture 1, vision and graphics (slide 8).

body.zh: 相机把光变成电信号，计算机存下的是数：灰度图是 高 × 宽 的二维数组，每格是一个像素的亮度；彩色图多一维通道，是 高 × 宽 × 3 的张量，每个像素是 (R, G, B) 三个数。数组的形状先写高、再写宽。一个像素只说这里有多亮，不说这一点离相机多远。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 8、22）。
body.en: The camera turns light into a signal and the computer stores numbers: a greyscale image is a height × width array, each cell one pixel's brightness; a colour image adds a channel axis, a height × width × 3 tensor, each pixel three numbers (R, G, B). The shape lists height first, then width. A pixel says how bright a place is, not how far it is from the camera. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slides 8, 22).

body.zh: 图像坐标从左上角起、从 0 数：x 向右增大，y 向下增大，和数学课上 y 轴朝上的坐标不同。按数组读时先行后列，写成 I[y, x]；OpenCV 的尺寸却写成 (宽, 高)。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，像素坐标（幻灯片 26）。
body.en: Image coordinates start at the top-left corner and count from 0: x grows to the right and y grows downwards, unlike the upward y of school geometry. Read as an array, row comes first: I[y, x]; OpenCV, though, writes a size as (width, height). Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, pixel coordinates (slide 26).

body.zh: 针孔相机把三维点 (X, Y, Z) 投到离针孔 f 的像平面上：x = fX/Z，y = fY/Z（相似三角形）。同样大的物体越远像越小，焦距 f 越长像越大；像只定出 H/Z 的比，大而远和小而近成同一个像。讲义把像平面画在针孔前面，像不倒过来：这是坐标约定，不是传感器真正的位置。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 11、18）。
body.en: A pinhole camera projects a 3D point (X, Y, Z) onto the image plane at distance f from the hole: x = fX/Z, y = fY/Z (similar triangles). An object of a given size images smaller the farther it is and larger the longer f is; the image fixes only the ratio H/Z, so large-and-far and small-and-near image alike. The lectures draw the image plane in front of the hole, so the image is upright: a coordinate convention, not where the sensor really is. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slides 11, 18).

body.zh: 针孔小，进光少，图暗；把孔开大，同一点的光落到传感器上的不同地方，图就糊。透镜让大孔进来的光重新会聚到一点，但只对对焦距离上的点会聚得准，别的距离的点在传感器上成一个模糊圈。光圈直径管进光量，焦距管像的大小，两者不能混。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，相机为什么需要透镜（幻灯片 12–13）。
body.en: A small pinhole lets in little light and the image is dark; widen the hole and light from one point lands at different places on the sensor, and the image blurs. A lens brings the light through a wide opening back to a point, but only for points at the focus distance; points at other depths make a blur circle on the sensor. The aperture diameter sets the light, the focal length the image size; the two are not to be confused. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, why cameras need lenses (slides 12–13).

body.zh: 同时显得清晰的深度范围。光圈小，模糊圈小，景深大，但进光少；光圈大，进光多，景深窄。摄影上用 f 数 = 焦距 / 光圈直径表示光圈：70 mm 镜头在 f/5.6 时光圈直径约 12.5 mm，f/32 的光圈更小、景深更大。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，光圈与景深（幻灯片 16）。
body.en: The range of depths that look sharp at once. A small aperture makes small blur circles and a deep range but lets in little light; a large aperture lets in more light and the range narrows. Photography states the aperture as the f-number = focal length / aperture diameter: a 70 mm lens at f/5.6 has an aperture of about 12.5 mm, and f/32 is a smaller aperture with a deeper range. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, aperture and depth of field (slide 16).

body.zh: 传感器大小一定时，焦距决定看得多宽：焦距短，视场大；焦距长，视场小，物体在图里显得大。图像宽 2000 像素、主点居中、焦距 1000 像素时，每边约 45°，视场约 90°。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，焦距与视场（幻灯片 15）。
body.en: With the sensor size fixed, the focal length decides how wide the camera sees: a short focal length gives a wide field of view, a long one a narrow view in which objects look larger. For an image 2000 pixels wide with the principal point in the middle and a focal length of 1000 pixels, each side covers about 45° and the field of view is about 90°. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, focal length and field of view (slide 15).

body.zh: 像平面上的长度以毫米计，图像里的长度以像素计，两者靠传感器的尺寸换算（每个像素多少毫米）。以像素计的焦距就是物理焦距除以像素尺寸。物体在 20 mm、200 像素高的传感器上占 100 像素，就是 10 mm：先换成毫米，再代入 h/f = H/Z。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲与 workshop 2。
body.en: Lengths on the image plane are in millimetres and lengths in the image in pixels; the sensor's size converts one to the other (millimetres per pixel). The focal length in pixels is the physical focal length divided by the pixel size. An object covering 100 pixels of a sensor 20 mm and 200 pixels tall is 10 mm tall on it: convert to millimetres first, then use h/f = H/Z. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 and workshop 2.

body.zh: 彩色图三个通道怎么排没有统一约定：OpenCV 读图得到 BGR，Matplotlib 按 RGB 显示。顺序弄错，红和蓝对调，形状和尺寸都不变；换顺序只是重排通道，不改图像的内容和大小。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，通道顺序（幻灯片 25）与 workshop 2。
body.en: There is no single convention for ordering a colour image's three channels: OpenCV reads images as BGR, Matplotlib displays them as RGB. Get the order wrong and red and blue swap while the shape and size stay; reordering only rearranges the channels and changes neither content nor size. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, channel ordering (slide 25), and workshop 2.

body.zh: 像素值有范围和类型：uint8 是 0 到 255 的整数，白是 255；处理时常换成 [0, 1] 的浮点数，好做加减乘除、不溢出。计算结果可以超出范围，显示时才把超出的值截到两端，存着的数不变：看上去一样白的两个像素，存的数可以不同。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，像素坐标、数据类型与文件格式（幻灯片 26）。
body.en: Pixel values have a range and a type: uint8 holds whole numbers from 0 to 255, white being 255; processing often converts to floats in [0, 1] so that arithmetic works without overflow. Results may leave the range; only the display clips them to its ends, and the stored numbers stay: two pixels that look equally white can hold different values. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, coordinates, data types and file formats (slide 26).

body.zh: 缩放一张图，要给新图的每个像素算出值，先得知道它在原图里的位置：在新图上铺一张采样网格，把每个新像素反向映射回原图的坐标，而不是把旧像素正向搬过去（那样放大时会留下空洞）。本课按像素中心对齐（OpenCV 的双线性缩放、PyTorch 的 align_corners=False 也这样）：宽从 m 变成 n 时，新像素 x 对应原图的 (x + 0.5)·m/n − 0.5。库与库的约定不同，所以要写明。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 34）。
body.en: To resize an image every new pixel needs a value, and first a position in the original: lay a sampling grid over the new image and map each new pixel back to coordinates in the original, rather than pushing old pixels forwards (which leaves holes when enlarging). This course aligns pixel centres, as OpenCV's bilinear resize and PyTorch's align_corners=False do: when a width m becomes n, new pixel x sits at (x + 0.5)·m/n − 0.5 in the original. Libraries differ in this convention, so it must be stated. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slide 34).

body.zh: 每个新像素复制原图里离它最近的那个像素的值。快，边缘硬，但放大后成块，缩小时整列整行的像素被丢掉，比取样间隔细的细节整个消失。离两边一样远时按约定取坐标较大的一边。它和裁剪不同：裁剪只取出已有的像素，不改尺寸。OpenCV 里叫 INTER_NEAREST。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 35）。
body.en: Each new pixel copies the value of the original pixel nearest to it. It is fast and keeps edges hard, but enlarging makes squares and shrinking drops whole rows and columns, so detail finer than the sample spacing vanishes. When a position is equally far from two pixels, the convention takes the larger coordinate. Unlike cropping, which takes existing pixels without resizing. OpenCV calls it INTER_NEAREST. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slide 35).

body.zh: 新位置落在两个相邻像素之间、离左边那个的距离是 t（0 ≤ t < 1）时，值取两边按距离的加权平均：(1 − t)·I[x0] + t·I[x0 + 1]。权重之和为 1，离得越近权重越大，所以新值介于两边之间，不只是照抄某一个旧像素。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 36，一维的情形）。
body.en: When a new position lies between two neighbouring pixels at distance t from the left one (0 ≤ t < 1), its value is their distance-weighted average: (1 − t)·I[x0] + t·I[x0 + 1]. The weights sum to 1 and the nearer pixel weighs more, so the new value lies between the two instead of copying one old pixel. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slide 36, the one-dimensional case).

body.zh: 在二维里，新位置落在四个旧像素之间；横向距离为 H、纵向距离为 V 时，四个权重是 (1−H)(1−V)、H(1−V)、(1−H)V、HV，和为 1，等于先沿 x、再沿 y 各做一次线性插值。它比最近邻平滑，却会把很锐的边变软，还会在标签图上造出不存在的值。双三次和 Lanczos 看更大的邻域，没有一种插值对每个任务都最好。OpenCV 里叫 INTER_LINEAR。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 36–37）。
body.en: In two dimensions a new position falls among four old pixels; with horizontal distance H and vertical distance V the four weights are (1−H)(1−V), H(1−V), (1−H)V and HV, summing to 1 — the same as linear interpolation along x and then along y. It is smoother than nearest neighbour but softens very sharp edges and invents values that do not exist in a label map. Bicubic and Lanczos look at larger neighbourhoods; no interpolation is best for every task. OpenCV calls it INTER_LINEAR. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slides 36–37).

body.zh: 传感器的信号最后存成有限个取值：uint8 每个值是 0 到 255 的整数，共 256 级。把实数存成 L 级，先把它截到可表示的范围，再取最近的一级（四舍五入，不是截掉小数）。不同的值会落到同一级，量化丢掉的信息找不回来。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（数据类型、uint8 的范围）。
body.en: The sensor's signal ends up stored as finitely many values: in uint8 each value is a whole number from 0 to 255, 256 levels. Storing a real number in L levels first clips it to the representable range, then takes the nearest level (rounding, not cutting off the fraction). Different values fall into one level, and what quantisation discards cannot be recovered. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (data types, the uint8 range).

body.zh: 取原数组的一个子区域，已有的像素值原样保留，不算新值；缩放改变数组的大小，要给新位置算出值。NumPy 里写成 image[y0:y0+h, x0:x0+w]。中心裁剪的起点是 x0 = ⌊(W − w)/2⌋、y0 = ⌊(H − h)/2⌋。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 34）与 workshop 2。
body.en: Takes a sub-region of the original array and keeps its pixel values as they are, computing nothing new; resizing changes the array's size and must compute values for the new positions. In NumPy it is image[y0:y0+h, x0:x0+w]. A centre crop starts at x0 = ⌊(W − w)/2⌋, y0 = ⌊(H − h)/2⌋. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slide 34) and workshop 2.

body.zh: 图的宽与高之比。把 768×512 直接压成 512×512 会改变宽高比，物体变胖或变瘦；要保持比例，宽和高乘同一个比例（缩到约 512×341），要的形状再用裁剪取出。OpenCV 的尺寸写成 (宽, 高)，NumPy 的形状是 (高, 宽, 通道)，两者不能照搬。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 34）与 workshop 2。
body.en: An image's width over its height. Squashing 768×512 straight into 512×512 changes it, and objects grow fatter or thinner; to keep proportions, scale width and height by one factor (to about 512×341) and take the wanted shape with a crop. OpenCV writes a size as (width, height) while a NumPy shape is (height, width, channels); one cannot be passed as the other. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slide 34) and workshop 2.

body.zh: 回答「整张图主要是什么」：给整张图一个或少量类别标签（dog），不说物体在哪里，也不说有几个。讲义也叫识别。检测再给每个物体一个位置，分割把答案细化到每个像素。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲，视觉任务（幻灯片 7）。
body.en: Answers what the image mainly shows: one or a few class labels for the whole image (dog), saying neither where the objects are nor how many there are. The lectures also call it recognition. Detection adds a position for each object, and segmentation refines the answer down to each pixel. Source: COMP90086 lecture 1, vision tasks (slide 7).

body.zh: 框住一个物体的矩形，用左上角和右下角两个像素坐标写出，例如 (4, 10)–(20, 26)。检测给每个物体一个类别和一个边界框；只有框、没有类别，说了在哪里，没说是什么。框只给出大致的范围，哪些像素属于物体要由分割回答。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲，视觉任务（幻灯片 7）。
body.en: The rectangle around an object, written as two pixel coordinates, its top-left and bottom-right corners, such as (4, 10)–(20, 26). Detection gives each object a class and a bounding box; a box without a class says where but not what. A box gives only the rough extent: which pixels belong to the object is for segmentation to answer. Source: COMP90086 lecture 1, vision tasks (slide 7).

body.zh: 给每个像素标出它属于哪一类（道路、天空、人）。它只说「哪一类」，不说「哪一个」：同一类的几个物体挨在一起时连成一片，从图上数不出个数。要分开同类的各个物体，用实例分割。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲，视觉任务（幻灯片 7）。
body.en: Labels each pixel with the class it belongs to (road, sky, person). It says which class, not which object: touching objects of one class merge into one region, and the map cannot tell how many there are. Telling apart the objects of one class is instance segmentation. Source: COMP90086 lecture 1, vision tasks (slide 7).

body.zh: 和图像一样大的一张图，每格是那一点离相机的距离，例如以米计。它是三维恢复的一种输出，回答「多远」。它的数是长度，可以比较远近、相减；类别图和实例图里的数是编号，不能当距离用。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲，视觉任务（三维恢复，幻灯片 7）。
body.en: A map as large as the image whose every cell holds that point's distance from the camera, in metres say. It is one output of 3D reconstruction and answers 'how far'. Its numbers are lengths, which can be compared and subtracted; the numbers in a class map or an instance map are ids and cannot serve as distances. Source: COMP90086 lecture 1, vision tasks (3D reconstruction, slide 7).

body.zh: 刻意扰动过的输入：只改动很少的像素，人眼几乎看不出变化，却能让神经网络把一个数字判成另一个数字，或把 dog 判成 hot dog，而且置信度很高。它说明模型在常见的照片上答得好，不等于它对输入的变化鲁棒。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，对抗样本（幻灯片 2–3）。
body.en: An input perturbed on purpose: a few altered pixels, a change the eye hardly sees, make a neural network read one digit as another or a dog as a hot dog, and with high confidence. It shows that answering ordinary photos well does not make a model robust to changes in its input. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, adversarial examples (slides 2–3).

body.zh: 已知物体、材质、灯光和相机，向前生成一张图像：这是正问题。计算机视觉走反方向，从图像推测这些东西。实际系统常把两者放在一起：按当前的估计渲染一张预测图，和真实的图比较，再用差异修正估计，叫 render and compare。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲，视觉与图形学（幻灯片 8）。
body.en: Given objects, materials, lights and a camera, generate an image forwards: a forward problem. Computer vision goes the other way, inferring these from the image. Real systems often combine the two: render a predicted image from the current estimate, compare it with the real one and correct the estimate by the difference — render and compare. Source: COMP90086 lecture 1, vision and graphics (slide 8).

body.zh: 一个物体挡在另一个前面，被挡住的部分在图像里没有一个像素。它是识别难的原因之一：同一个物体露出的部分不同，看上去就不同。被整个挡住的东西，图像既不能证实，也不能否定，连「它不在场景里」也说不出。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲，识别为什么难（幻灯片 28）。
body.en: One object stands in front of another, and the hidden part has no pixel at all in the image. It is one reason recognition is hard: one object looks different depending on what part of it shows. Of something entirely hidden the image can confirm nothing and deny nothing — not even that it is absent from the scene. Source: COMP90086 lecture 1, why recognition is hard (slide 28).

body.zh: 数字图像的一格。灰度图里一个像素是一个数，说那里有多亮；彩色图里是几个数，每个通道一个。像素只记下亮度和颜色，不记下这一点离相机多远。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，成像与图像张量（幻灯片 8、22）。
body.en: One cell of a digital image. In a greyscale image a pixel is one number, how bright that place is; in a colour image it is several numbers, one per channel. A pixel records brightness and colour, not how far that point is from the camera. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, image formation and the image tensor (slides 8, 22).

body.zh: 彩色图比灰度图多出的那一维：每个像素按通道存几个数，最常见的是红、绿、蓝三个。三个通道是相机和人眼视觉的工程表示（人眼有三类主要的视锥细胞），不是说自然界只有三种颜色。取出一个通道，得到的是一张灰度图。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，图像张量（幻灯片 22）。
body.en: The axis a colour image has beyond a greyscale one: each pixel stores one number per channel, most often three, for red, green and blue. Three channels are an engineering representation shared by cameras and human vision (the eye has three main kinds of cone), not a claim that nature has only three colours. One channel taken out is a greyscale image. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, the image tensor (slide 22).

body.zh: 常用的开源计算机视觉库，Python 里写作 cv2。用它时要记住它自己的约定：尺寸写成 (宽, 高)，和 NumPy 数组的形状 (高, 宽, 通道) 相反；cv2.imread 读进来的彩色图按 BGR 排通道；缩放的插值方式有 INTER_NEAREST、INTER_LINEAR 等。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲与 workshop 2。
body.en: A widely used open-source computer vision library, cv2 in Python. Its own conventions must be kept in mind: a size is written (width, height), the reverse of a NumPy array's shape (height, width, channels); cv2.imread reads colour images with their channels in BGR order; its resizing interpolations include INTER_NEAREST and INTER_LINEAR. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 and workshop 2.

body.zh: 针孔相机里光线穿过针孔后落上的平面，讲义也叫成像平面；它离针孔的距离是焦距 f。真实相机的传感器在针孔后面，像是倒的；讲义把像平面画在针孔前面，像不倒过来，也省掉负号。这是坐标约定，不是传感器真正的位置。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，针孔相机与成像模型（幻灯片 11、18）。
body.en: The plane that rays reach after passing a pinhole camera's hole, at the focal length f from it. In a real camera the sensor is behind the hole and the image is upside down; the lectures draw the image plane in front of the hole, so the image is upright and the minus signs go away. This is a coordinate convention, not where the sensor really is. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, the pinhole camera and the image formation model (slides 11, 18).

body.zh: 针孔相机里是针孔到像平面的距离 f，透镜相机里是镜头的焦距。它管像的大小，和管进光量的光圈直径是两个不同的长度，不能混为一谈。像平面上它以毫米计，在数字图像里常换成以像素计。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，针孔相机与透镜（幻灯片 11、13）。
body.en: In a pinhole camera, the distance f from the hole to the image plane; in a lens camera, the lens's focal length. It sets the image size and is a different length from the aperture diameter, which sets the light; the two are not to be confused. On the image plane it is in millimetres; for digital images it is often converted to pixels. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, the pinhole camera and lenses (slides 11, 13).

body.zh: 镜头放光进来的开口，大小用直径 D 表示（台上记作 A）。它管进来多少光；管像的大小的是焦距。光圈小，接近针孔，进光少；光圈大，进光多。摄影上用 f 数写光圈。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，透镜与光圈（幻灯片 13、16）。
body.en: The opening through which a lens lets light in, its size given as the diameter D (A on the bench). It sets how much light comes in; the image size is the focal length's business. A small aperture comes close to a pinhole and lets in little light; a large one lets in more. Photography writes the aperture as an f-number. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, lens and aperture (slides 13, 16).

body.zh: 一点射出的光经过透镜，在传感器上落成的那个小圆，也叫弥散圆。点在对焦距离上时，它缩成一点；不在时，它有一定大小，这一点就显得糊。模糊圈小于一个门槛（比如一个像素的大小）时，就算清晰。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，相机为什么需要透镜（幻灯片 12–13）。
body.en: The small disc that the light from one point makes on the sensor after the lens, also called the circle of confusion. For a point at the focus distance it shrinks to a point; otherwise it has some size and the point looks blurred. A blur circle below a threshold, such as one pixel's size, counts as sharp. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, why cameras need lenses (slides 12–13).

body.zh: 摄影上写光圈的方式：f 数 = 焦距 / 光圈直径，写成 f/2、f/5.6、f/32。同一支镜头，f 数越大，光圈越小。70 mm 镜头在 f/5.6 时，光圈直径约为 70/5.6 = 12.5 mm。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，光圈与景深（幻灯片 16）。
body.en: Photography's way of writing the aperture: f-number = focal length / aperture diameter, written f/2, f/5.6, f/32. On one lens, the larger the f-number, the smaller the aperture. A 70 mm lens at f/5.6 has an aperture about 70/5.6 = 12.5 mm across. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, aperture and depth of field (slide 16).

body.zh: 光轴穿过像平面的那一点，像平面上量位置的起点。理想相机的主点在传感器正中，视场两边对称；真实相机的主点会有偏移，要和像素尺寸、镜头畸变一起考虑。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，针孔相机与焦距（幻灯片 11、15）。
body.en: The point where the optical axis meets the image plane, from which positions on the plane are measured. In an ideal camera it sits at the centre of the sensor and the field of view is symmetric; in a real camera it is offset and must be accounted for along with the pixel size and lens distortion. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, the pinhole camera and focal length (slides 11, 15).

body.zh: Python 的绘图库。matplotlib.pyplot.imshow 按 RGB 显示彩色图，所以 OpenCV 读进来的 BGR 图要先用 cv2.cvtColor(image, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB) 换通道顺序再显示；这一步只换顺序，不改内容和尺寸。出处：COMP90086 workshop 2。
body.en: Python's plotting library. matplotlib.pyplot.imshow displays colour images as RGB, so a BGR image read by OpenCV is first converted with cv2.cvtColor(image, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB); this changes only the channel order, not the content or the size. Source: COMP90086 workshop 2.

body.zh: 无符号 8 位整数，像素最常见的存法：每个值是 0 到 255 的整数，黑是 0，白是 255，RGB 里的纯红是 [255, 0, 0]。相加、相乘容易溢出，所以处理时常换成 float32 并缩到 [0, 1]，算完再明确地换回去。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲，数据类型（幻灯片 26）与 workshop 2。
body.en: The unsigned 8-bit integer, the commonest way to store pixels: each value a whole number from 0 to 255, black 0, white 255, pure red in RGB [255, 0, 0]. Sums and products overflow easily, so processing often converts to float32 scaled to [0, 1] and casts back explicitly at the end. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2, data types (slide 26), and workshop 2.

body.zh: Python 的数组库。图像在里面是一个数组，形状写成 (高, 宽, 通道)，下标先行后列：image[y, x]。切片 image[y0:y0+h, x0:x0+w] 取出一块；切片返回的常是原数组的视图，要单独修改时先 .copy()。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲与 workshop 2。
body.en: Python's array library. An image is an array whose shape is written (height, width, channels), indexed row first: image[y, x]. The slice image[y0:y0+h, x0:x0+w] takes out a region; a slice is often a view of the original array, so copy it with .copy() before changing it on its own. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 and workshop 2.
